newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFin prices firm, freeze concerns remain.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFin prices firm, freeze concerns remain.

text.p: Dealers bid up prices of Russian MinFin bonds on Monday, encouraged by a planned Eurobond offering and a Moscow prosecutor's announcement which gave a hard figure to the amount of bonds frozen in a recent scandal.
But trading remained relatively thin and dealers said the the freeze had been factored into prices, not dismissed.

A detective from the Moscow's district prosecutor office told Reuters on Monday it had issued an order to freeze $56.81 million in face value of bonds in June, bringing the total bonds currently known to have been frozen to $74 million.
The finance ministry in July announced that $24 million had been frozen, including six million announced again on Monday.
Officials at Vneshtorgbank, the main MinFin depositary, declined to comment on the prosecutor's statement.
Dealers said rumours on the issue had been circulating for a week. "We knew it all, this has been priced in already," one dealer said.
National Reserve Bank dealer Andrei Ivanov-Golitsyn said the news had pacified the market.
"Market (liquidity) is far below what we had some weeks ago, but it is better than last week, and prices are likely to rise over the next few days."
Traders said the market's liquidity was seen higher.
More banks, including those from abroad, had traded directly on Monday, they said. Last week deals were generally made through brokers in order to decrease counterparty risk.

Ivanov-Golitsyn said the market also lifted on news that Russia's long-awaited Eurobond issue is expected by the end of November and that President Boris Yeltsin's health is satisfactory ahead of heart surgery expected early this week.
